title: Normalized open-extension Roos comparison on arbitrary strict towers
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each small pro-etale site put $B_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and use the ordinary unbounded module derived category $D(B_W)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Open extension and restriction mean exact ringed-slice functors $e_!\dashv e^*$, applied termwise [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact].
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-open-immersion]. Work with sites small in the fixed module universe; all tower indices are $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. Write $L_W=R\lim$ for total right derived inverse limit on strict towers of $B_W$-modules and use its normalized signed Roos model [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. A strict tower complex $M_\bullet$ has termwise product $P_M=\prod_nM_n$, transition shift $s((x_n)_n)=(d_nx_{n+1})_n$, and signed fiber $\mathsf H(M)^a=P_M^a\oplus P_M^{a-1}$ with differential $(x,y)\mapsto(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$. Here $d_n:M_{n+1}\to M_n$ are the tower transitions. Denote termwise extension by $J$ and termwise restriction by $G$; the same open operations on derived categories are written $j_!$ and $j^*$.
Then $U,X$ are Noetherian and qcqs, $j$ is quasi-compact, and $\ell$ is invertible on both schemes. The exact ringed extension $j_!$ has invertible canonical countable-product comparison $\phi_M:j_!\prod_nM_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_nj_!M_n$, characterized by $\mathrm{pr}_n\phi_M=j_!(\mathrm{pr}_n)$; countable products of $B_U$-modules and $B_X$-modules are exact.
For every strict tower complex $M_\bullet$ on $U$ there is a specified natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_M:j_!L_UM_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}L_XJM_\bullet.$$
Its representative under the normalized Roos identifications is $\phi_M$ on both signed summands of $\mathsf H(M)$; it is independent of resolutions. For every complex $D$ of $B_U$-modules and strict augmentation $c:\Delta D\to M_\bullet$, let $a_c:D\to L_UM_\bullet$ denote its actual induced map. Then
$$\lambda_M\circ j_!(a_c)=a_{Jc}:j_!D\longrightarrow L_XJM_\bullet.$$
Here $\Delta$ is the constant tower, and both augmentations have first Roos coordinate $(c_n)_n$ and shifted coordinate zero. All assertions are natural in strict tower maps and strict augmentation squares. No separatedness of $X$ over $k$, boundedness or constructibility of $M_\bullet$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit to $F=j_!$ on these two small ringed sites. Define $\lambda_M=\theta_{JM}^{-1}\kappa_M j_!(\theta_M)$ using its normalized signed Roos isomorphisms. Its statement gives an isomorphism natural in strict tower maps, represented by $\phi$ on both signed summands and independent of resolutions. The categories here are the ordinary unbounded module derived categories, so this application imposes no boundedness or constructibility condition.

proof.text: The generic strict-limit theorem supplies signed augmentation maps b and b-prime with first coordinate gamma and shifted coordinate zero, and proves their comparison equality. To identify these with the actual induced maps through every K-injective resolution, first construct the canonical inclusion from the ordinary limit into the signed Roos complex. Signed coordinates uniquely determine it. Use the normalization-on-injectives and naturality along a functorial K-injective resolution to prove eta theta = Q(iota) at every complex, using the normalized_unit argument of lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-roos-resolution. The coordinate equations imply b = a0 iota for the ordinary strict-limit augmentation a0. On any K-injective I, eta_I is invertible because ordinary limit preserves homotopy equivalences. Set dI = eta_I followed by the inverse of L(Qq), and a = a0 followed by lim(q). Limit projections and naturality of eta prove exactly the three resolution-normalized augmentation equations in ComparisonAssertions. Repeat this for the extended tower; functoriality preserves its strict compatibility equation.

Step 3: every hypothesis of lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit holds: ringed product φ for a quasi-compact open with a small family, exact countable products on U and X, exact additive j_! Edge cases U=∅, U=X, zero tower and identity-transition tower all pass.
